articles.title: Previsão do tempo BH: Chuva no fim de semana e frente fria | G1
articles.standfirst: Inmet prevê pancadas de chuva, trovoadas e possibilidade de granizo no sábado (7) e no domingo (8). Na capital, temperaturas podem chegar a 32°C antes da chegada do frio.
articles.summary: Previsão do tempo em BH alerta para chuva e granizo no fim de semana antes de frente fria em Minas Gerais derrubar as temperaturas para 12°C nos próximos dias.
articles.body:
A chuva deve continuar neste fim de semana em Belo Horizonte e na Região Metropolitana. Segundo o Instituto Nacional de Meteorologia (Inmet) , a previsão para sábado (7) e domingo (8) é de pancadas de chuva e trovoadas isoladas, com possibilidade de granizo e rajadas de vento de até 60 km/h. A chegada de uma frente fria também deve provocar queda nas temperaturas nos próximos dias.

No sábado, o tempo deve permanecer abafado, com aumento da nebulosidade e pancadas de chuva principalmente a partir da tarde. Em Belo Horizonte, as temperaturas devem variar entre 19°C e 32°C, segundo a previsão do Inmet para a estação da Pampulha.

Já no domingo, a frente fria que avança pelo Sudeste deve deixar o céu nublado, com possibilidade de chuva a qualquer hora do dia. Na capital, a mínima prevista é de 19°C e a máxima, de 27°C.

O Inmet também alerta para a possibilidade de chuvas de 20 a 30 milímetros por hora ou até 50 milímetros por dia, acompanhadas de rajadas de vento entre 40 e 60 km/h e queda de granizo, em todas as regiões de Minas Gerais durante o fim de semana.

Imagem da Praça da Liberdade, em Belo Horizonte, durante a chuva na tarde desta quinta-feira (5) — Foto: Reprodução/TV Globo

A partir de segunda-feira (9), a massa de ar frio que acompanha a frente fria deve provocar uma queda mais acentuada nas temperaturas em Minas Gerais.

Em Belo Horizonte, a previsão é de mínima de 14°C e máxima de 20°C na segunda-feira, com céu nublado a parcialmente nublado e chuva isolada.

Na terça-feira (10), os termômetros devem cair ainda mais, com mínima de 12°C e máxima de 18°C. O céu deve ficar parcialmente nublado, com possibilidade de chuva isolada.

De acordo com o Inmet, a queda nas temperaturas é considerada atípica para novembro e caracteriza um episódio de frio tardio, embora de intensidade amena.

A previsão de mais chuva ocorre após uma semana marcada por temporais em Belo Horizonte e na Região Metropolitana.

Na quinta-feira (5), a chuva forte provocou alagamentos , quedas de árvores e danos a imóveis na capital e em cidades vizinhas, como Santa Luzia e Contagem.

Segundo dados da Defesa Civil de Belo Horizonte, as regiões Noroeste e Oeste registraram, cada uma, 50,6 milímetros de chuva entre 12h e 16h30 de quinta-feira. O volume equivale a mais de 20% da média esperada para todo o mês de novembro, que é de 236 milímetros.

Na manhã de sexta-feira (6), seis regionais da capital estavam sob alerta de risco geológico forte , válido até segunda-feira (9): Venda Nova, Norte, Nordeste, Pampulha, Noroeste e Oeste.

A Defesa Civil orienta que a população evite áreas sujeitas a alagamentos, não atravesse ruas inundadas e não se abrigue debaixo de árvores durante tempestades. Em caso de emergência, o órgão pode ser acionado pelo telefone 199.

articles.title: O que se sabe sobre modelo brasileiro encontrado morto na França | G1
articles.standfirst: Rafael Pereira Modesto, de 39 anos, era natural de Uberlândia, no Triângulo Mineiro, e trabalhava como modelo e estilista na França. Família tenta trazer o corpo para o Brasil, mas ainda não recebeu informações sobre a causa da morte.
articles.summary: Rafael Pereira Modesto foi achado em seu apartamento na França após dias sem contato; família de Uberlândia busca R$ 50 mil para trazer o corpo ao Brasil.
articles.body:
Rafael Pereira Modesto foi encontrado morto no sábado (31) — Foto: Reprodução/Redes Sociais

O modelo brasileiro Rafael Pereira Modesto , de 39 anos, foi encontrado morto no apartamento onde morava, em Paris, na França , no sábado (31). Natural de Uberlândia , no Triângulo Mineiro, ele vivia na Europa desde os 18 anos e trabalhava com moda.

A morte foi descoberta depois que familiares passaram cerca de uma semana sem conseguir falar com ele. Enquanto tenta esclarecer as circunstâncias do caso, a família também busca recursos para trazer o corpo ao Brasil.

Veja abaixo o que se sabe sobre o caso e quais informações ainda não foram esclarecidas.

Rafael foi encontrado morto no apartamento onde morava, em Paris , no sábado (31). O último contato dele com a família ocorreu em 23 de outubro.

Segundo a madrasta, Juliana Costa, o modelo mantinha contato frequente com a mãe, a irmã e a avó, geralmente todos os dias ou, no máximo, a cada dois dias.

Após uma semana sem notícias, os parentes ficaram preocupados e pediram ajuda a uma amiga que também mora na França para verificar se estava tudo bem.

A mulher foi até o apartamento, mas não conseguiu falar com Rafael. Bombeiros e policiais franceses foram acionados, arrombaram a porta do imóvel e encontraram o corpo do brasileiro.

"Foi desesperador. A gente ficou sem saber, mandando mensagens, tentando contato com alguém lá que pudesse falar alguma coisa dele e saber onde ele morava. Foi tudo muito difícil", contou Juliana.

Natural de Uberlândia, Rafael deixou o Brasil aos 18 anos para realizar o sonho de conhecer o mundo. Ao longo dos anos, morou em diferentes países da Europa até se estabelecer em Paris.

Aos 39 anos, trabalhava como modelo e estilista. Segundo a madrasta, ele era apaixonado por moda, gostava de viajar e tinha planos de conhecer novos lugares. Atualmente, não tinha emprego fixo.

Juliana conhecia Rafael havia cerca de 25 anos e acompanhou parte da infância e da adolescência dele. Ela o descreveu como uma pessoa alegre, ambiciosa e muito ligada à família.

Mesmo morando longe, ele mantinha contato frequente com os parentes e demonstrava preocupação principalmente com a saúde dos pais e da avó. Recentemente, chegou a conversar mais vezes com o pai depois que ele teve pneumonia.

Rafael completaria 40 anos no dia 4 de dezembro.

Rafael atuava como modelo e estilista — Foto: Reprodução/Redes Sociais

A família ainda não havia recebido informações sobre a causa da morte até a última atualização desta reportagem.

Também não foram divulgados detalhes sobre as circunstâncias em que Rafael foi encontrado no apartamento. Os familiares aguardam esclarecimentos das autoridades francesas.

"Não temos conhecimento da causa da morte e a família também não possui nenhuma suspeita ou confirmação de suicídio. Até o momento, não tivemos acesso às informações oficiais que esclareçam as circunstâncias do falecimento", afirmou a cunhada de Rafael, Mariana Palomino.

A família ainda busca respostas sobre o que provocou a morte do modelo e aguarda informações sobre os procedimentos necessários para a liberação do corpo.

Nenhum detalhe sobre a investigação conduzida pelas autoridades francesas foi divulgado, nem se há previsão para a conclusão dos procedimentos.

Quando o corpo será levado para o Brasil?

A família pretende trazer o corpo de Rafael para Uberlândia, onde vivem os parentes e onde ele nasceu. No entanto, o traslado internacional envolve despesas com documentação e transporte.

Segundo Juliana, os custos devem chegar a aproximadamente R$ 50 mil. Diante do valor, os familiares iniciaram uma campanha de arrecadação por Pix, que havia reunido cerca de R$ 9 mil até a última atualização.

Uma cunhada do modelo ficou responsável por manter contato com o consulado brasileiro e buscar orientações sobre os procedimentos necessários.

"Nosso objetivo nesse momento é conseguir trazer o corpo dele de volta. A gente queria muito que tivesse um auxílio do governo, nem falo financeiro, mas que fosse lá e ajudasse a resolver, porque é um custo muito alto", afirmou Juliana.

Em nota, o Ministério das Relações Exteriores (Itamaraty) informou que, por meio do Consulado-Geral do Brasil em Paris, tem conhecimento do caso e está em contato com a família, a quem presta assistência consular.

Os familiares esperam que Rafael seja velado e enterrado em Uberlândia, cidade onde nasceu e onde viveu com os parentes no bairro Segismundo Pereira.

Família não sabe a causa da morte de modelo — Foto: Reprodução/Redes Sociais

Como funciona o registro de óbito de um brasileiro no exterior?

1. O óbito é registrado na embaixada ou consulado brasileiro

O registro deve ser feito na representação brasileira responsável pelo país onde ocorreu a morte.

A declaração deve ser feita, de preferência, por um familiar, como cônjuge, filho, irmão, mãe ou pai.

Em alguns casos, um representante autorizado, como uma funerária, também pode realizar o procedimento.

Entre os principais documentos exigidos estão:

formulário de registro de óbito preenchido;

certidão de óbito emitida pelas autoridades locais;

documento de identidade brasileiro do falecido;

documento de identidade do familiar ou representante que fizer a declaração.

A emissão da certidão consular de óbito não tem custo.

4. O documento precisa ser validado no Brasil

Depois de ser emitida pela embaixada ou pelo consulado, a certidão deve ser transcrita em um cartório de registro civil no Brasil para ter validade legal.

Como funciona o translado do corpo para o Brasil?

Além do registro de óbito, também é necessário emitir e legalizar outros documentos, entre eles:

autorização para o transporte internacional do corpo;

atestado sanitário comprovando que a morte não foi causada por doença contagiosa.

Em casos de doenças infectocontagiosas, o corpo deve ser transportado em uma urna metálica hermeticamente fechada.

🔎Os órgãos onde as certidões, certificados e atestados são emitidos variam conforme o país.

Segundo o Itamaraty, o governo brasileiro não custeia despesas como:

translado do corpo ou das cinzas para o Brasil;

Em regra, esses custos são de responsabilidade da família ou de pessoas e instituições que decidam prestar apoio financeiro.

articles.title: Pajubá, Caetano confuso e funk: as questões que marcaram o Enem | G1
articles.standfirst: Pergunta sobre duas músicas de Caetano Veloso fez até o cantor ficar em dúvida entre as alternativas. Em matemática, 'enigma' com poucas informações no enunciado viralizou: 'cadê o resto?'.
articles.summary: Pergunta sobre duas músicas de Caetano Veloso fez até o cantor ficar em dúvida entre as alternativas. Em matemática, 'enigma' com poucas informações no enunciado viralizou: 'cadê o resto?'.
articles.body:
Um enunciado de matemática praticamente sem números, uma música que mistura Bach e pancadão, trechos de canções sobre os quais o próprio cantor não soube responder, uma campanha enigmática de entrar Fernando e sair Pessoa, e até o pajubá, conjunto de expressões associado à comunidade LGBTQIA: é preciso dizer que o Exame Nacional do Ensino Médio (Enem) é eclético.

Todos os tópicos listados acima apareceram em edições da prova nos últimos anos e tornaram-se, por diferentes razões, motivo de debate nas redes sociais.

Enquanto a edição de 2026 não começa, o g1 montou este #TBT abaixo. Será que você conseguiria acertar as questões?

Nem Caetano Veloso chegou à resposta de primeira

Questão do Enem 2023 cita canções de Caetano Veloso — Foto: Reprodução/Inep

No Enem 2023, uma questão de linguagens colocou lado a lado duas músicas de Caetano Veloso: "Alegria, Alegria" e "Anjos Tronchos". O que as letras têm em comum?

A repercussão foi tamanha que Paula Lavigne, mulher do cantor, filmou o marido tentando resolver o desafio (veja o vídeo mais abaixo).

Ao ler as alternativas, Caetano reagiu: "Quando li, achei que são todas corretas". Depois de analisar melhor as opções, ficou dividido entre duas respostas: B e D.

O gabarito oficial considerou que a certa era a letra B, que abordava a percepção da profusão de informações gerada pela tecnologia.

Pois é. Nem o autor conseguiu identificar imediatamente a resposta esperada pelo exame. Pobres candidatos.

A questão de matemática que parecia estar incompleta

Questão de matemática do Enem 2024 viraliza nas redes sociais — Foto: Reprodução/Redes sociais

Um estudante havia calculado a média de quatro provas, mas, por engano, dividiu a soma das notas por cinco. Com isso, chegou a um resultado uma unidade menor do que a média correta.

Até aí, tudo bem. O problema, na visão de muitos candidatos, era que o enunciado não apresentava nenhuma das notas nem o valor da média calculada.

A reação nas redes sociais foi imediata. No X, antigo Twitter, usuários compartilharam fotos da questão com comentários como "Cadê o resto?" e "Como você quer que eu saiba?".

Mas havia uma solução: bastava montar uma equação de primeiro grau a partir das informações fornecidas.

O raciocínio levava à alternativa B, que indicava média correta igual a 5.

Pajubá no Enem virou alvo de crítica de Bolsonaro

Enem 2018 - Prova Amarela - Pergunta 31 — Foto: Reprodução

O conjunto de expressões reúne termos associados historicamente a gays, travestis e drag queens.

A presença do tema na prova provocou reação do então presidente eleito Jair Bolsonaro. Na época, ele criticou a abordagem e afirmou que o Enem deveria cobrar história e cultura do Brasil, e não uma questão relacionada à temática LGBT.

O episódio ganhou repercussão política, mas a abordagem de diferentes variedades e usos da língua portuguesa está entre os conteúdos tradicionalmente cobrados pelo exame.

Questão sobre 'Entrar Fernando e sair Pessoa' viralizou no Enem — Foto: Reprodução

Na prova de linguagens do Enem 2025, um cartaz de divulgação da Bienal do Livro chamou a atenção dos candidatos com uma frase: "Você entra Fernando. E sai Pessoa".

A peça publicitária mostrava um jovem com a cabeça preenchida por referências à cultura portuguesa, como bondinhos e caravelas. A mensagem fazia uma brincadeira com o escritor Fernando Pessoa e com a ideia de transformação provocada pela leitura.

Nas redes sociais, a questão gerou discussões sobre qual seria a interpretação correta da imagem e da frase.

O gabarito oficial do Inep apontou a alternativa C: ressaltar o impacto da leitura na vida das pessoas.

Mas os candidatos entraram na sala de prova otimistas e saíram confusos.

De Bach ao funk: o fenômeno 'Bum Bum Tam Tam'

Questão sobre Bum bum tam tam caiu no Enem 2020 — Foto: Reprodução

No Enem 2020, outra questão musical chamou a atenção dos candidatos. Desta vez, o protagonista era MC Fioti e seu sucesso "Bum Bum Tam Tam".

A música, que se tornou um fenômeno nas plataformas digitais, utiliza um trecho de uma composição do alemão Johann Sebastian Bach. O detalhe curioso é que Fioti produziu a faixa sozinho, em uma noite, e contou que nem sequer sabia quem era o compositor da melodia original.

Na prova, os candidatos precisavam identificar o processo de criação musical presente na mistura de referências tão diferentes.

A resposta correta era a letra E: a inter-relação de elementos culturais provenientes de realidades distintas na construção de uma nova proposta musical.

Em outras palavras, era preciso reconhecer o encontro entre a música erudita de Bach e o funk brasileiro. Os candidatos tiveram de rebolar para resolver.

Depois de Caetano, pajubá, Fernando Pessoa e MC Fioti, fica a curiosidade: qual será a questão que vai virar assunto nas redes sociais na edição deste ano?

Talvez uma pergunta sobre a questão 67 de alguma cor de prova?

articles.title: Estudante de medicina no Paraguai fica sem dinheiro para mensalidade | G1
articles.standfirst: Vinicius Eduardo mora há três anos no Paraguai e trabalha no Brasil para custear os estudos. Com dinheiro bloqueado no Ueno Bank, estudante tenta conseguir adiantamento salarial para pagar a faculdade.
articles.summary: Vinicius Eduardo mora há três anos no Paraguai e trabalha no Brasil para custear os estudos. Com dinheiro bloqueado no Ueno Bank, estudante tenta conseguir adiantamento salarial pa
articles.body:
O brasileiro Vinicius Eduardo Nunes Pereira da Silva, estudante de medicina em Cidade do Leste no Paraguai, ficou sem acesso ao dinheiro que havia reservado para pagar a mensalidade da faculdade após a quebra do Ueno Bank, um dos maiores bancos digitais do país . Com o pagamento próximo do vencimento, ele tenta conseguir um adiantamento salarial para não ficar inadimplente e correr o risco de perder as provas.

“Para mim foi muito inesperado, porque como eu tenho dia certo pra pagar minha mensalidade, num dia tava o dinheiro lá, daí no outro dia quando eu vou ver já tá bloqueado, não consigo nem mostrar meu saldo. A gente fica desamparado", relatou.

Na terça-feira (3), o Banco Central do país suspendeu as operações do Ueno Bank , após identificar problemas na situação financeira da instituição, deixando clientes, incluindo brasileiros, sem acesso ao dinheiro depositado.

Na quinta-feira (5), o Banco Central do Paraguai começou a pagar os primeiros valores aos clientes do Ueno Bank. Na primeira etapa de devolução, cerca de 722 mil correntistas, que tinham até 10 milhões de guaranis depositados, o equivalente a R$ 8,8 mil, vão receber o dinheiro de volta. Até o momento, 197.191 milhões de guaranis paraguaios foram devolvidos, o equivalem a aproximadamente R$ 176 milhões.

Vinicius Eduardo perdeu o acesso à conta bancária — Foto: RPC Foz do Iguaçu

Vinicius mora no Paraguai há cerca de três anos e trabalha em Foz do Iguaçu, no Brasil, para pagar a faculdade, o aluguel e as despesas do dia a dia. Ele conta que foi surpreendido pelo bloqueio da conta, sem conseguir consultar o saldo ou movimentar o dinheiro.

A preocupação do estudante é que, segundo ele, a faculdade exige que os alunos estejam com as mensalidades em dia para participar das avaliações. Caso não consiga pagar dentro do prazo, Vinicius afirma que terá de arcar com custos adicionais para fazer as provas posteriormente.

Sem previsão de quando poderá recuperar o dinheiro, ele tenta negociar um adiantamento com a empregadora no Brasil para conseguir quitar a mensalidade.

"Eu estou conversando com minha patroa lá do Brasil pra fazer um adiantamento pra eu conseguir fazer o pagamento."

Vinicius explica que abriu a conta no Ueno Bank para facilitar os pagamentos no Paraguai e economizar com as taxas de câmbio. Segundo ele, a alternativa permitia evitar gastos de R$ 50 a R$ 100 por mês com a conversão do dinheiro enviado do Brasil.

Ueno Bank no Paraguai — Foto: Marcos Landim/RPC

'Recebemos e acordamos no outro dia sem nada do dinheiro', diz mulher que teve valores bloqueados após quebra do Ueno Bank no Paraguai

articles.title: Candidatos do Enem tentam descobrir pistas da redação em posts do Inep | G1
articles.standfirst: Ministro da Educação afirmou, nesta quarta (4), que nem ele sabe qual será a proposta. Ainda assim, alunos alimentam a lenda de que o Inep dá indícios do tema nas semanas anteriores ao exame.
articles.summary: Ministro da Educação afirmou, nesta quarta (4), que nem ele sabe qual será a proposta. Ainda assim, alunos alimentam a lenda de que o Inep dá indícios do tema nas semanas anteriores ao exame.
articles.body:
Todo ano, a mesma saga: candidatos do Exame Nacional do Ensino Médio (Enem) analisam minuciosamente cada post nas redes sociais do Instituto Nacional de Estudos e Pesquisas Educacionais Anísio Teixeira (Inep) para encontrar pistas de qual será o tema da redação.

Stalkear os "paqueras" é coisa do passado. A moda agora é ter o feed do Inep decorado.

Cada escolha estética de quem administra o Instagram do órgão é examinada. Nesta edição, vários posts recentes tinham relação com avatar de videogame, por exemplo. Pronto, isso foi suficiente para alunos projetarem a proposta:

"Os impactos do vício em jogos eletrônicos na saúde física e mental dos jovens”.

No TikTok, há quem veja cada post do Inep como uma pista sobre a redação — Foto: Reprodução/Redes sociais

O ministro da Educação, Leonardo Barchini, deixou claro, em transmissão ao vivo desta quarta-feira (4), que o tema da redação é mantido sob sigilo — nem ele próprio fica sabendo antes qual tópico será cobrado.

"É sempre motivo de muita curiosidade. O ministro faz questão de nem passar perto", brincou Barchini.

Mas nada convencerá os alunos de que o estagiário de marketing não descobriu a informação secreta.

📱Vamos a uma outra teoria da conspiração. Com tantos posts com essência "retrô" e referências a celulares, o Inep estaria dando uma pista sobre temas de redação relacionados à tecnologia. Vídeos e mais vídeos no TikTok levantam possibilidades como:

"Os desafios para a regulamentação da inteligência artificial e seus impactos nas relações de trabalho no Brasil;"

"Os impactos da exposição precoce às tecnologias digitais na saúde mental de crianças e adolescentes no Brasil";

"Os impactos da hiperconectividade na saúde mental dos brasileiros".

Alguns são mais taxativos e iludem os candidatos com a falsa promessa de prever o tópico da redação. "O Inep está dando de bandeja o tema", diz uma influenciadora. "Simplesmente, o Inep está dando dicas do que vai cair na redação, mas você não está prestando atenção", diz outra.

Outros são mais honestos e explicam que absolutamente nada comprova ou já comprovou que o Inep poste dicas do tema . Mas entram na brincadeira e aproveitam para sugerir propostas que inspirem os candidatos a escrever dissertações nos moldes do Enem. Afinal, exercitar é sempre a melhor forma de se preparar para a prova.

Daniela Toffoli, professora de redação do Curso Anglo, reforça que o melhor caminho não é se dedicar a ter "uma bola de cristal".

"Ficar brincando de detetive atrapalha. O estudante vai gastar energia em torno disso, isso vai gerar ansiedade, e a aposta pode estar errada. O que faz a diferença é construir proposta de intervenção completa, estudar repertório por eixo temático e entender quais as competências avaliadas", afirma.

Posts do Inep com pixels aparentes já levantaram hipótese de redação sobre tecnologia — Foto: Reprodução/Redes sociais

🔍Quais outros temas foram cogitados por quem colocou uma lupa nos posts do Inep?

Educação e segurança na escola foram outros temas cogitados nas redes — Foto: Reprodução/Redes sociais

Postagens sobre acessibilidade no Enem já geraram a especulação sobre temas relacionados a pessoas com deficiência:

"Caminhos para combater as barreiras físicas, comunicacionais e atitudinais enfrentadas por pessoas com deficiência no Brasil";

"Desafios para garantir a inclusão e a cidadania de pessoas com deficiência no Brasil".

Educação também foi a aposta de usuários das redes sociais, depois que o Inep publicou conteúdos sobre alfabetização e importância da leitura:

"Desafios para a alfabetização de crianças no Brasil";

"Desafios para a formação de leitores no Brasil contemporâneo";

"Perspectivas para democratizar o acesso à leitura no Brasil".

E o terceiro tema ventilado pelos candidatos foi violência na escola, porque o órgão do MEC abordou esse assunto em posts sobre ações de combate ao bullying:

"Perspectivas para a construção de uma cultura de paz e de convivência nas escolas brasileiras";

"Desafios para combater o bullying e promover uma cultura de respeito nas escolas brasileiras".

O Instagram do Inep deu alguma pista real nos últimos anos?

'Teorias da conspiração': posts do Inep daria dicas do tema da redação do Enem? — Foto: Reprodução/Redes sociais

Há quem dê uma forçada de barra e diga que, no Enem 2025, o tema "Perspectivas acerca do envelhecimento na sociedade brasileira" havia sido anunciado de modo velado nas redes sociais do Inep, porque "postaram gatinhos e imagens de 'bom dia' que idosos mandam no zap".

Convenhamos que seja uma associação não tão imediata...

Algo indica, portanto, que as previsões de 2026 estejam corretas? Não. Não há evidências "científicas", apenas um folclore enemziano.

"Nenhum levantamento confiável mostra que posts anteciparam, de fato, o tema. Em 2024, por exemplo, muita gente esperava que a redação fosse sobre tecnologia ou meio ambiente, por causa das redes sociais do MEC e do Inep, mas acabou sendo sobre valorização da herança africana", diz Toffoli, do Anglo.

Mas é aquela história: todos os temas cogitados acima seguem o estilo de propostas do Enem. Nada impede que, por coincidência, algum deles esteja correto.

➡️Só não se deixe levar pela ilusão de que saber o tópico abordado é garantia de nota boa. O importante, como já reforçou a professora Daniela Toffoli, não é se desgastar tentando prever o futuro, e sim treinar bastante e dominar as regras da prova: saber construir uma proposta de intervenção com todos os elementos obrigatórios, escolher repertórios culturais produtivos e elaborar parágrafos com encadeamento de ideias, por exemplo.

articles.title: Happy Choti Diwali 2026: Images, Wishes, Messages, Greetings, and Status Updates to Share on WhatsApp, Instagram and Facebook
articles.summary: There’s something truly magical about Diwali.
articles.body: There’s something truly magical about Diwali. As the air fills with a familiar buzz, homes everywhere start glowing with rows of diyas, festive lights, and bursts of color. And just before the main festival, Choti Diwali comes along, ushering in a fresh wave of excitement, hope, and togetherness. Known by different names across India, like Naraka Chaturdashi, Roop Chaudas, and Kali Chaudas, Choti Diwali is a celebration steeped in stories of victory, renewal, and the power of even the smallest light to push away darkness.Choti Diwali isn’t just a warm-up act for Diwali’s grand spectacle. It’s a meaningful day all on its own, packed with rituals, family gatherings, and a sense of cleansing — both body and spirit. Lighting tiny diyas, making rangoli, sharing sweets, and swapping greetings have a way of bringing people closer than ever. It’s a chance for everyone to pause, look around, and send a bit of joy to the people who matter most. Sometimes, all it takes is a heartfelt message, a cheerful status update, or a simple greeting to make someone’s festival brighter.If you’re on the hunt for a special wish or image for Choti Diwali 2026, I’ve put together a bunch of greetings, messages, and catchy status ideas you can post on WhatsApp, Instagram, Facebook, or wherever you like spreading festive cheer.When is Choti Diwali 2026: The date and what makes it specialChoti Diwali 2026 happens on Sunday, November 8. This year, thanks to the alignment of the lunar calendar, some places will celebrate Choti Diwali and the main Diwali festival on the same date. Here’s how it works: as per the Hindu Panchang, Chaturdashi Tithi starts at 10:47 am on November 7 and ends at 11:27 am on November 8. That means the traditional Abhyanga Snan, a sacred oil bath, takes place on the morning of November 8. Since timings can vary based on where you’re celebrating, always check your local Panchang or festival calendar for the right time slots.Depending on where you are in India, you’ll hear Choti Diwali go by different names. In the North, it’s usually “Choti Diwali,” while many states call it Naraka Chaturdashi. Roop Chaudas rings familiar in parts of western India, and Gujaratis say Kali Chaudas. In Maharashtra, everyone wakes up early for Abhyanga Snan, making it a key part of the festival. Down south, Naraka Chaturdashi often stands as the main Diwali celebration itself.The roots of this festival run deep in ancient myth. At its center is the story of Narakasura, a fearsome demon king. When his misdeeds grew unbearable, Lord Krishna (with help from Satyabhama) defeated Narakasura and freed those he had wronged. The legend reminds us: no matter how strong the darkness, it can’t overshadow the power of goodness or bravery. Lighting lamps, sharing sweets, and gathering with loved ones all circle back to this message of hope and triumph.How do people celebrate Choti Diwali?Traditions shift from one region to another, but the heart of Choti Diwali beats with the same vibrant message: wash away the old, bring in the new, and celebrate goodness taking the lead.First up is Abhyanga Snan. Early in the morning, before sunrise, families take a special oil bath. They rub on herbal ubtan, which is believed to purify the body and mind. Freshly washed and in new clothes, they gather for prayers and start the day's celebrations.Then come the diyas. People dot their entrances, windows, and courtyards with tiny flame-lit lamps. The glow says “welcome” and pushes out negative energy. Prayers often go out to Lord Krishna, Goddess Lakshmi, and Lord Yama.In Goa, the festival gets even more eye-catching. Giant effigies of Narakasura dominate the night, only to be set ablaze in the early hours, which is a powerful (and dramatic) symbol of evil’s defeat.Back at home, people whip up sweet treats and snacks, exchange gifts, and spend time with their loved ones. Colorful rangolis brighten up doorsteps. Really, Choti Diwali is all about sharing traditions and making space for joy together.Wishes and messages for Choti Diwali 2026If you want to brighten someone’s day, be it family, friends, or colleagues, here are messages that go beyond the standard “Happy Diwali!” Try these on WhatsApp, post them on Instagram, or send them in a card:1. May every diya light up your path and every smile bring you joy! Wishing you and your family a bright, beautiful Choti Diwali!2. Here’s to new beginnings, sweet surprises, and moments that turn into memories… Shubh Choti Diwali!3. Light the diyas for hope, and let joy chase the shadows away. Happy Naraka Chaturdashi!4. Every lamp you light today brings double the happiness tomorrow. Wishing you warmth, laughter, and love this Choti Diwali.5. May your worries melt away, your dreams take flight, and your days be full of brightness. Have a safe and happy festival!6. Let Goddess Lakshmi bless your home, Lord Ganesha clear your path, and the festival bring peace to your heart.7. The glow of diyas, the sweetness of treats, and the company of loved ones — may these fill your days with joy.8. Choti Diwali reminds us: hope always finds a way. Here’s to countless reasons to celebrate.Heartfelt greetings for family and loved onesFestivals mean more when family is around, even if it’s just in spirit. These wishes add a little extra love for the people you hold close.1. Home feels extra special when we’re together! Wishing my family a joyful Choti Diwali packed with laughter and memories.2. May health, happiness, and togetherness forever fill our home. Each diya brings us closer… Happy Choti Diwali!3. Warm hugs and festive wishes to the ones who light up my life. May your days shine like Diwali lights.4. Decorations can’t replace the warmth of family. Here’s to a home filled with kindness, peace, and happiness.5. articles.body: HYDERABAD: A 23-year-old student from Nalgonda district, who is pursuing her master’s degree at the University of Massachusetts (UMass) in the US, has gone missing in Boston. According to local police, Sreeja Reddy Koya was last seen leaving her residence in Dorchester, near Edison Green, at around 9.45 pm on Nov 2 for an evening walk.The incident came to light after her friends alerted the police when she failed to return from the walk. Her phone's location reportedly indicated an area near a beach, but her whereabouts remain unknown.The Boston Police Department has issued a missing-person alert, seeking the public's assistance in tracing Sreeja. According to the alert, she may be in the vicinity of Carson Beach or Harbor Point.“The Boston Police Department is actively working to locate Sreeja Koya and urges anyone with information regarding her whereabouts to call 911,” a notice on the department's website stated.The University of Massachusetts has also made an appeal on social media, seeking information about its missing student.According to the university’s notice, “Koya was seen wearing a black jacket, grey jeans and no shoes.” The notice further stated that she “may be experiencing a mental health crisis and is known to frequent the Carson Beach and Harbor Point areas”.Sreeja is the daughter of Koya Yadagiri Reddy and Roopa, residents of Shabdullapuram village in Kanagal mandal of Nalgonda district. She moved to the US in 2025 to pursue a MS degree and is expected to complete the course in about six months, according to sources. Her parents are worried and anxiously awaiting information about their daughter’s whereabouts.Local media reports said Sreeja had attended classes on the day she went missing, completed her part-time job and returned to her accommodation, which she shares with other Telugu students.Roads and buildings minister Komatireddy Venkat Reddy has urged the Indian embassy, the ministry of external affairs (MEA), Boston police and other officials concerned to coordinate their efforts and ensure that Sreeja is traced safely. articles.title: France deploys 70,000 security personnel ahead of fresh nationwide protests
articles.summary: French trade unions and student groups are set to stage another day of protests across the country on Saturday, while the Yellow Vests movement plans a
articles.body: French trade unions and student groups are set to stage another day of protests across the country on Saturday, while the Yellow Vests movement plans a separate rally in central Paris despite a ban by authorities.The demonstrations follow weeks of youth-led unrest and nationwide strikes over the rising cost of living and public services.The protests come less than six months before France elects a new president to replace centrist leader Emmanuel Macron, who cannot seek another term.The far right is leading in opinion polls, while the unrest has put pressure on Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu ahead of a meeting with trade unions and employers' organisations on Monday.Student groups and trade unions have called for an authorised march in central Paris "against the high cost of living and in support of young people".The Yellow Vests activists, however, have refused to join the march and instead called for a separate rally at Place de la Concorde, near the lower house of parliament and the presidential palace, despite the authorities' ban.Interior minister Laurent Nunez said 70,000 police officers and security personnel would be deployed across France."If there are any rioters or looters... we'll be ready and waiting for them," he said.Yellow Vests call for 'mass disobedience'The Yellow Vests movement, which staged protests eight years ago against planned fuel-tax hikes under Macron's government, has called on supporters to go ahead with the banned rally."We are calling for mass disobedience," Benjamin Ball, a member of the movement's coordinating committee, said.The demonstrations in recent weeks have been largely peaceful, although clashes with police and vandalism have occurred on their sidelines. France witnessed its worst rioting in years on October 17, prompting authorities to impose curfews, ban large gatherings and restrict protest routes.On Thursday, hundreds of thousands of workers took part in nationwide strikes and demonstrations. The interior ministry said the protests had "generally gone well" despite 642 arrests, while clashes were reported in several cities.According to Reuters, the interior ministry put Thursday's nationwide protest turnout at 575,000, while the CGT trade union, one of the organisers, estimated that 1.6 million people had participated.The ministry also said 53 police officers were injured and 448 people arrested during the demonstrations.In Paris, police fired tear gas after clashes broke out at the front of the march, while some demonstrators and police also clashed as the protest wound down. In Lyon, riot police fired tear gas and charged a group of protesters.Unions demand wage rises and better conditions for young peopleThe unions are demanding an increase in the minimum wage, which has not received a discretionary boost since 2012, across-the-board wage rises, tax reforms and better learning conditions for young people."The only thing that will bring the protests to an end is a response to the demands that have been put forward for several weeks by workers, civil servants, young people and pensioners," an inter-union coalition said on Friday.Lecornu is due to discuss wages and purchasing power with representatives of trade unions and employers' organisations on Monday.The latest unrest has brought workers and students together in demonstrations over living costs, public services and education.The one-day strike on Thursday also involved some energy workers and teachers, while just over 15 per cent of teaching staff joined the strike, according to the education ministry.The protests have also drawn criticism of police tactics, with dozens of internal investigations launched into allegations of brutality against demonstrators. The government has defended the police response while saying allegations of abuses would be investigated.France's economy, the second-largest in the European Union, is under pressure to rein in public debt, limiting the government's scope to meet protesters' demands.You use AI every day. articles.title: US midterm setback puts Vance at forefront of renewed Iran diplomacy
articles.summary: US vice president JD Vance has taken the lead in backchannel talks with Iran over the past two weeks, seeking to revive a ceasefire and restart stalled
articles.body: US vice president JD Vance has taken the lead in backchannel talks with Iran over the past two weeks, seeking to revive a ceasefire and restart stalled nuclear negotiations.According to Axios, Vance has held near-daily discussions with Qatari Prime Minister Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman Al-Thani, Pakistan's Chief of Army Staff Field Marshal Asim Munir and other regional mediators to push negotiations forward.Vance's involvement comes as the Trump administration explores a diplomatic way out of the conflict, which the vice-president had opposed before it began. He has also linked the war to the Republican Party's losses in this week's US midterm elections.US President Donald Trump is allowing diplomatic efforts to continue to see whether a deal with Tehran is possible, although the US military remains prepared to resume strikes at relatively short notice if negotiations fail."We're talking to them," Trump told reporters on Friday when asked about his message to Iran.Qatari Prime Minister Sheikh Mohammed said efforts to prevent further escalation had continued through coordination with officials in Washington and Tehran."For the past couple of weeks we have worked with colleagues in the US administration who have a genuine intention to find a way to contain the situation and to de-escalate it. Thanks to them and thanks to wise voices in Tehran we prevent it from getting out of control," he said.He added that talks with the Trump administration had continued after the midterm elections, although they had become less active as Washington dealt with other priorities. The US administration's intention to find a diplomatic solution, he said, remained unchanged and a deal was possible.Vance had opposed war, pushed for diplomacyVance was among the most sceptical voices in Trump's inner circle before the conflict began at the end of February, advocating a diplomatic solution instead of military action.He later led the US negotiating team at an April summit on Iran in Islamabad and was personally involved in discussions that resulted in a US-Iran memorandum of understanding (MOU) in June.The vice-president subsequently headed the American delegation for direct talks with Iran in Switzerland. The discussions ended with Tehran agreeing to invite UN inspectors to visit its nuclear facilities.However, the understanding collapsed shortly afterwards when Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps resumed attacks on ships.Two weeks ago, Vance wrote to Mohsen Rezaei, secretary of Iran's Supreme National Security Council, proposing a return to direct negotiations.You use AI every day. articles.title: ‘E20 turned into 420’: Rahul Gandhi alleges petrol samples from Karnataka exceed 20% ethanol limit
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Lok Sabha LoP and Congress leader Rahul Gandhi on Saturday alleged that petrol companies were supplying fuel with ethanol content exceeding the
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Lok Sabha LoP and Congress leader Rahul Gandhi on Saturday alleged that petrol companies were supplying fuel with ethanol content exceeding the mandated 20% limit, citing laboratory tests of samples collected from seven districts in Karnataka.In a post on X, Gandhi claimed that 11 of the 14 petrol samples tested at an accredited laboratory contained more than 20% ethanol. He cited samples from Indian Oil Corporation (IOCL) and Hindustan Petroleum Corporation (HPCL), which allegedly recorded ethanol levels of 31.2% and 30.5%, respectively."E20 turned into 420 - stealing petrol from the public's cars!" Gandhi said, accusing both government-owned and private oil companies, including IOCL, HPCL, BPCL, Nayara and Shell, of exceeding the prescribed limit.He also alleged that the companies' own laboratories had failed to report the ethanol content in the samples.Challenges for a debateQuestioning the impact on consumers, Gandhi said higher ethanol blending could affect vehicle mileage and increase maintenance costs, claiming that cars not designed to handle such fuel could suffer damage.He further questioned the absence of clear labelling at petrol pumps, arguing that consumers were not being given information about the actual ethanol content of the fuel they purchased."You're paying for expensive petrol, but ethanol is being pumped into your tank. Who loses out? You," he said.Also read: More than 30% ethanol in E20, says Karnataka ministerGandhi asked Prime Minister Narendra Modi to clarify the actual ethanol content in petrol supplied across the country and explain what action would be taken against companies allegedly exceeding the 20% limit."Modi ji, tell us - what's being put in the country's tank? How much ethanol is actually in the petrol? When will action be taken against companies mixing more than 20% ethanol?" he asked.The Congress leader also reiterated his challenge to debate the government, saying the issue of ethanol blending would be added to the discussion on whose interests the government's policies serve.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: Shaurya squadron to change how India's tank formations will fight future wars
articles.summary: After artillery and infantry, the Armoured Corps of the Indian Army is now working to operationalise drones within the organic structure of its regiments
articles.body: After artillery and infantry, the Armoured Corps of the Indian Army is now working to operationalise drones within the organic structure of its regiments through the Shaurya Squadron. The Army, in the midst of a modernisation drive, is working towards becoming a more agile fighting force. As part of this change, the force is reshaping and adopting newer structures, units and sub-units in response to the evolving nature of combat. Some of these structural changes include the formation of Integrated Battle Groups (IBGs), the raising of Bhairav battalions and the formation of Ashni platoons for the infantry. Other changes have also been announced, such as the Shaktibaan Regiment and Divyastra Battery, both of which will be part of the artillery.What is the Shaurya SquadronThe new sub-unit, will be the fifth squadron of an armoured regiment, as per a source close to the issue. Currently, an armoured regiment has three sabre squadrons equipped with tanks and a headquarter squadron. The headquarters squadron also contains the regiment's reconnaissance (recce) troop. As per the source, the recce troop will form the core of the new squadron and will also have drones for both observation and strike roles. Apart from this the new squadron could also be equipped with light tanks, according to the source.The introduction of this squadron will expand the ability of the armoured regiment to see better, this increased level of situational awareness is expected to improve the combat effectiveness of the army's armoured spearhead in both offensive and defensive operations. Each operational command of the army has an armoured regiment that is working to fine tune the use of in its own operational environment, as per the source.The concept first came to light in March this year at Exercise Amogh Jwala, when the then southern army commander and now army chief General Dhiraj Seth was briefed on it. Pune-based southern command said the embryonic squadron was tested under realistic battlefield conditions, combining precision strikes with deep surveillance and close-combat reconnaissance. It was designed, the command said, to "seek further, strike deeper and stay longer", showing that real-time reconnaissance can be paired with a quick, precise strike.It surfaced again in July, when Lieutenant General Rajesh Pushkar, the present General Officer Commanding-in-Chief of Southern Command, visited the 31 Armoured Division, also known as the White Tiger Division, which demonstrated its capabilities and briefed him on new equipment.Part of a wider drone structureThe Armoured Corps is following the infantry and the artillery. The Army has raised its first dedicated drone battalion, the Baaz Battalion, under 11 Corps (Vajra Corps) in Jalandhar, on the western front with Pakistan. Unlike the smaller drone platoons embedded in infantry units, it is designed to operate a wider range of platforms, including Searcher drones and long-endurance systems such as the MQ-9B, Heron and Hermes. It is expected to act as a hub for flight management, maintenance, software updates, data exploitation and coordination with troops, with artificial intelligence-based decision-support systems helping to process the data.For the infantry, Ashni platoons will provide battalions with their own drones for reconnaissance and offensive operations. The artillery is preparing Divyastra batteries and Shaktibaan regiments, which will use longer-range drones and loitering munitions. These sit alongside Integrated Battle Groups and Bhairav battalions, and the Shaurya Squadron extends the same approach to armour.Protecting the tankThe changes draw on lessons from the standoff with China along the Line of Actual Control, Operation Sindoor in May 2025, and the wars in Ukraine and West Asia, where drones have been used for reconnaissance, artillery targeting and direct attack. Armies have responded by adding roof protection, including cage-like structures, along with electronic countermeasures and active protection systems. Camouflage, concealment, dispersal and mobility have again become important for armoured formations.These changes fit into a wider shift towards multi-domain operations under a joint doctrine issued by the headquarters integrated defence staff in August 2025, which seeks to combine satellite imagery, drone feeds, electronic intelligence and artillery targeting to speed up battlefield decisions. The new formations signal a move away from manpower-heavy structures towards a network-centric force in which infantry, artillery and armour use unmanned systems as part of their routine operations, while being able to defend against the same threats from an adversary.

articles.title: Cancer in India: Screening exists, but why are patients still diagnosed late
articles.summary: Cancer in India is often detected late.
articles.body: Cancer in India is often detected late. By the time many patients are diagnosed, the disease has already advanced, when treatment is harder and the chances of survival are lower. Part of the explanation lies in how screening is organised in the country, and part lies in how people respond to early warning signs.The stakes are considerable. The Indian Council of Medical Research’s National Cancer Registry Programme estimated 13.92 lakh new cancer cases in India in 2020, up from 13.25 lakh in 2018, and about 7.7 lakh cancer deaths in 2020, according to figures the Union Health Ministry placed before Lok Sabha. The question that follows is how many of these cases could have been caught sooner.A public programme that exists, and a habit that has not formedIndia does run a public screening system. The National Programme for Prevention and Control of Cancer, Diabetes, Cardiovascular Diseases and Stroke, now called the National Programme for Prevention and Control of Non-Communicable Diseases (NP-NCD), was launched in 2010 in 100 districts across 21 states. In 2016, population-based screening was added for everyone aged 30 and above. It covers hypertension, diabetes and three cancers: of the oral cavity, the cervix and the breast.The design is meant to bring screening close to the community. Under the Health Ministry’s guidelines, an ASHA worker completes a Community Based Assessment Checklist. People aged 30 to 65 are then offered an oral visual examination and, for women, a clinical breast examination and a visual inspection of the cervix with acetic acid. Each is meant to be repeated once in five years. The ministry’s training module for staff nurses estimates that in a population of 1,000, about 370 people are eligible for oral cancer screening and about 182 women each for breast and cervical screening. The cervical test is offered at the primary health centre level to begin with.What the national survey foundUptake is low. The fifth National Family Health Survey, conducted between 2019 and 2021, asked adults aged 30 to 49 whether they had ever been screened for cancer. Among women, 1.9 per cent reported ever having had a cervical cancer screening test, 0.9 per cent a breast examination and 0.9 per cent an oral cavity examination. Among men, 1.2 per cent reported ever having had an oral cancer examination.The variation between states was wide. Tamil Nadu recorded the highest rates for cervical and breast screening, at 9.8 per cent and 5.6 per cent respectively. Cervical screening stood at 0.2 per cent in Gujarat, Assam and West Bengal, and in at least half of the states and Union Territories fewer than one per cent of women had ever been screened for it.Why cancers are found lateDr Prasad’s explanation has two parts. India has no mandatory screening programme, he said, and patients often ignore early signs, so they are diagnosed only when the disease is at an advanced stage.The Health Ministry’s 2016 operational framework for cancer screening makes the same point about late detection. It says cancers in India tend to be detected late, leaving little room for effective treatment, and cites five-year survival of 60.2, 76.3 and 73.2 per cent for early-stage oral, breast and cervical cancers, against 3.3, 14.9 and 7.9 per cent at an advanced stage. The figures come from a 2010 population-based study.The framework also stresses that screening is not an end in itself. It needs assured treatment, regular follow-up and linkages between every level of care, so that a person who tests positive can reach confirmation and treatment.Who should be screened, and whenDr Prasad’s recommendations differ from what the public programme offers, and he set them out group by group.As per the guidelines, Dr Prasad said, women should begin breast cancer screening at 40. Women who are sexually active should be tested from 21, mainly to prevent cervical cancer. Men between 45 and 50 can have a Prostate Specific Antigen test once a year. Men and women alike should have a colonoscopy once every 10 years from the age of 50. From 40, he said, both men and women should mandatorily undergo a master health screening.The two differ in scope, age and frequency. The national framework’s screening protocols cover three cancers, oral, breast and cervical, for people aged 30 to 65, at five-year intervals; prostate and colorectal cancers are not among them. The framework itself notes that breast screening yields much more in women over 40, but keeps the starting age at 30 for programmatic and operational reasons.Vaccination and cervical cancerDr Prasad also pointed to vaccination against cervical cancer for girls aged 9 to 14, which he said can prevent cervical cancer in women by up to 95 to 98 per cent. The Union Budget speech of February 2024 had announced that the government would encourage vaccination for girls in that age group.The national HPV vaccination campaign was launched in February 2026. It offers a free, voluntary, single-dose vaccine to 14-year-old girls, with parental consent, at government health facilities. The Health Ministry puts the annual cohort of 14-year-olds at about 1.2 crore girls, citing Registrar General of India estimates.By 11 September 2026, more than 80 lakh doses had been administered, the ministry said. Gujarat, Uttar Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh and Mizoram reported 100 per cent coverage of their identified target groups, while Bihar, Andhra Pradesh and Assam had crossed 90 per cent. Uttar Pradesh had vaccinated more than 22 lakh girls, the highest of any state.The barrier he names: AwarenessAsked whether cost, fear, lack of awareness or access keeps people from being screened, Dr Prasad said it is mainly lack of awareness, along with the belief that nothing will happen to them. “Anything can happen to anyone at any point of time,” he said.The Health Ministry’s 2016 framework makes a related point. Because awareness of health is low, it says, screening for conditions with no obvious symptoms is seen as unnecessary, particularly among the poor, for whom a day’s visit to a secondary or tertiary facility can mean a lost day’s wages. On the cost of treatment, the Health Ministry has told Parliament that care in government hospitals is either free or highly subsidised for the poor and needy.The urban and rural gapIn cities, Dr Prasad said, access and availability are plentiful, and a person with symptoms can reach cancer care. In tier two and tier three cities the best cancer care may not be available, he said, but screening is available in almost all government colleges and hospitals. Where tier one cities hold a clear advantage is awareness, because their residents have easier access to information about screening.The public cancer care network is meant to narrow the rest of the distance. Under the central government’s scheme for strengthening tertiary care for cancer, 19 State Cancer Institutes and 20 Tertiary Care Cancer Centres have been approved. The Centre and states share the cost in a 60:40 ratio, and 90:10 for the North-Eastern and hilly states, according to a reply in Rajya Sabha. In the Union Budget for 2025-26, the Finance Minister said the government would facilitate day-care cancer centres in all district hospitals over three years, with 200 to be set up in 2025-26.The case for a yearly check-upAsked for the one change that would do the most, Dr Prasad proposed mandatory health check-ups, once a year or at least once in two years, for everyone working in the government and private sectors.He expects the benefit to travel beyond the employee. This should also help in getting family members checked, he said, as many of them will come forward for testing. Cancer screening under the national programme, by comparison, is meant to be repeated once in five years.What it will takeThe pieces are not missing. A public programme offers screening for three cancers to people aged 30 to 65. A vaccination campaign is reaching 14-year-old girls through government facilities, and the Budget has announced day-care cancer centres for district hospitals. What the 2019–21 survey shows is a gap between what is offered and what people take up, with fewer than two in every hundred women aged 30 to 49 having ever been screened for cervical cancer.Dr Prasad’s account of that gap is a simple one: people do not think it can happen to them.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: Luxon fights to stay as New Zealand concludes elections
articles.summary: Polls closed in New Zealand on Saturday after the final day of voting in what is expected to be one of the country's tightest elections in years.
articles.body: Polls closed in New Zealand on Saturday after the final day of voting in what is expected to be one of the country's tightest elections in years. The early results are due shortly after the ballot ended.Prime Minister Christopher Luxon's conservative National Party is seeking a second term against a left-wing bloc led by Labour leader Chris Hipkins. With neither side having a clear path to victory, smaller parties are expected to play a crucial role in deciding who forms the next government.Voting ended at 7pm local time after polling began on October 26. New Zealand's Electoral Commission aimed to release an initial count covering 5% of the votes within 30 minutes of polling stations closing. Results from 95% of ballots cast are expected by the end of Saturday night. The final verified tally, including overseas votes, is due on November 27.The closely fought contest has left both the right-wing and left-wing blocs uncertain about their prospects. Pre-election opinion polls suggested neither major grouping was likely to secure a straightforward parliamentary majority.Luxon, who took office in 2020, is seeking another term after facing two confidence votes among his own lawmakers this year. Hipkins, meanwhile, is attempting to return to power after Labour suffered a decisive defeat in the 2023 election.Economic concerns dominate campaignThe cost of living and economic difficulties have been central issues during the campaign. New Zealand's trade-dependent economy has struggled with the impact of international shocks, while unemployment in the September quarter reached its highest level in 15 years.National formed a coalition with two right-wing parties, populist New Zealand First and libertarian ACT, after winning the 2023 election. The alliance produced the country's most conservative government in modern history.Luxon, a former business executive who entered parliament in 2020, has faced criticism over his political inexperience compared with the leaders of his coalition partners. Both minor parties have secured significant policy concessions from the prime minister.On the other side, Labour is seeking to regain ground with the support of the Green Party and Te Pati Maori, an Indigenous rights group.Hipkins, a career politician, became prime minister nine months before the 2023 election after Jacinda Ardern stepped down. However, Labour has struggled to recover its popularity since its electoral defeat. Hipkins also continues to face criticism over pandemic-era policies introduced under the previous government.Minor parties could hold key to government formationNew Zealanders do not directly elect their prime minister. Instead, voters cast two ballots, one for their preferred political party and another to elect their local representative.A party or coalition must secure more than half the seats in parliament to form a government. The final number of seats is determined through official calculations based on the country's electoral system.If neither major bloc secures enough support, parties could be forced into negotiations to form a coalition. Previous election deadlocks have seen the two sides compete to win the backing of smaller parties holding the balance of power.This time, The Opportunity Party could emerge as a potential kingmaker if it wins parliamentary representation for the first time.Led by 38-year-old Qiulae Wong, the centrist party is backed by candidates described as socially liberal technocrats. Its proposals include a land tax, universal basic income and environmental measures.Wong, who has a business background but no political experience, has pledged to negotiate first with whichever party secures the most votes if her party holds the balance of power.Luxon has ruled out forming a government with The Opportunity Party. However, analysts believe both major party leaders would be willing to negotiate with Wong if her support becomes essential to securing a parliamentary majority.You use AI every day. articles.title: A Texas refinery worker was exposed to asbestos over decades and later died of mesothelioma; his family's $325,000 punitive award was cut to $200,000, but the court also revived additional claims against the company
articles.summary: The Texas Court of Appeals has upheld a finding that a refinery company was grossly negligent in the asbestos-related death of a former worker, but
articles.body: The Texas Court of Appeals has upheld a finding that a refinery company was grossly negligent in the asbestos-related death of a former worker, but reduced his family's damages award from $325,000 to $200,000. In its November 5 ruling, the court also allowed the family to pursue additional claims against the company, sending them back for further proceedings.According to case details on Justia, The case concerns Louie Scudder, who worked at the La Gloria refinery in Tyler, Texas, for a total of 38 years. He first joined the refinery in 1958, left in 1964 and returned in 1966, continuing until 1998. He was diagnosed with mesothelioma in November 2019 and died on June 25, 2022, aged 83.His family alleged that years of exposure to asbestos at the refinery caused his illness and death. His son, Carl Christian Scudder, filed a lawsuit against Tyler MD Holdings LLC, the successor-in-interest to Tyler Holding Company, formerly known as La Gloria Oil and Gas Company.A jury found that asbestos fibres from the refinery had caused Scudder's illness and death. It also held the company grossly negligent and awarded his family $325,000 in exemplary damages. The company challenged the verdict, arguing that the evidence did not establish that Scudder's exposure at the refinery had caused his illness.What happened during his years at the refineryScudder's work involved several tasks that brought him into contact with insulation materials containing asbestos.As a maintenance helper, he sometimes drilled into insulated pipes and equipment to remove plugs. He also used a wrench to knock off pipe coverings. The court noted that these activities created dust.He helped insulation workers cut pipes and prepare insulating cement. Scudder estimated that he worked with insulation for about three hours a week. When he poured dry cement powder into a bucket and mixed it with water, it created visible dust.At other times, he helped clean insulation debris. He also spent about 15 minutes twice a week sweeping the insulation shop.Scudder told the court that before 1980, he did not recall receiving warnings about asbestos or training on how to handle it. He also did not remember being given a mask or respirator or seeing warning signs about asbestos at the refinery. He said he did not recall the refinery testing the air for asbestos.In 1989, he received a week's training on asbestos removal. He was taught about the risks, how to set up enclosed work areas and how to use protective clothing and a respirator. He was also shown how to collect and dispose of asbestos safely.Link between exposure and illnessTyler MD argued that Scudder's exposure at the refinery was too low to have caused his mesothelioma. It pointed out that the exposure levels calculated for him were below the limits permitted under workplace safety standards at the time.The family's industrial hygiene expert, Kenneth Garza, reviewed Scudder's work history and testimony. He calculated his asbestos exposure between 1972 and 1980 at 0.175. His calculation considered the work Scudder did, how often he did it, how long the tasks lasted and the level of exposure.Garza compared this estimate with studies involving people who performed similar work. He said Scudder's exposure represented more than a doubling of the risk of developing mesothelioma. One study indicated a 21-fold increase in risk, while two others showed increases of 2.8-fold and four-fold.The family's medical expert, Dr Edwin Holstein, told the court that Scudder's exposure at the refinery between 1972 and 1980 was a substantial factor in causing his mesothelioma and death. He also said he found no other cause for the illness apart from the asbestos Scudder inhaled at the refinery.The appeals court found that the family had presented enough evidence to support the jury's decision. It rejected the company's argument that exposure below workplace safety limits automatically meant it could not be held responsible for gross negligence.Court finds company failed to protect workersThe court also examined what the company knew about asbestos and the steps it took to protect employees.The judgment referred to evidence that the National Safety Council had discussed asbestos hazards in 1951. By 1966, it was specifically concerned about mesothelioma. Workplace safety rules covering asbestos were introduced in 1972.Scudder said he did not recall receiving asbestos warnings, safety training or protective equipment before 1980. The company's representative also acknowledged that workplace safety rules were known in the oil and gas industry during the 1970s.The court examined a company document dated June 22, 1979, which discussed monitoring asbestos in the air. However, the document did not include measurements or other data showing that such monitoring had been carried out.An inspection by the Texas Air Control Board on June 22, 1989, found that a sample of insulating material from a heat exchanger pad contained 45% to 50% asbestos. The court noted that Scudder had worked in that area.Another company document discussed the cost of removing asbestos. It said that $500,000 would not be enough for the work and that there was no comprehensive estimate for the project.The appeals court said the jury could have concluded that the company knew about the dangers of asbestos but did not take adequate steps to protect workers. It therefore upheld the finding of gross negligence.The court allowed more claimsThe family had also accused the company of negligence and other wrongful acts. However, a lower court had earlier dismissed these claims after accepting the company's argument that workers' compensation rules prevented the family from pursuing them.The appeals court found that the company had not provided enough evidence to show that it had the required workers' compensation insurance for the relevant years of Scudder's employment.It also noted that mesothelioma was not covered as an occupational disease under Texas law before an amendment took effect in August 1971. The court therefore reversed the earlier decision dismissing the family's additional claims and sent them back for further proceedings. This does not mean the company has been found liable on those claims.Why the damages were reducedThe jury had awarded the family $325,000 in exemplary damages. It had also found that Scudder's wife, Mary Ann, suffered $175,000 in past and future financial losses because of his death.However, the appeals court said the evidence did not support that amount. Mary Ann had told the court that Scudder handled household maintenance and gardening. After his death, she paid a man $40 to mow the lawn and carry out basic yard work.The court said her testimony supported a single payment of $40 but did not establish how often such services were needed or how much the other household work was worth. It found that the evidence was not enough to justify the $175,000 amount.Under Texas law, the court said the maximum exemplary damages in this case could not exceed $200,000. It therefore reduced the award from $325,000 to $200,000.The court sent the family's additional claims back for further proceedings while upholding the jury's finding that the company was grossly negligent.You use AI every day. articles.title: Utah millionaire father of seven built a 300-acre doomsday compound stocked with food, weapons and supplies to shelter 200 people if civilisation collapses; property now doubles as a TV filming location
articles.summary: If you've been watching Homestead on your phones and TVs, beware that there is more of where it's coming from.
articles.body: If you've been watching Homestead on your phones and TVs, beware that there is more of where it's coming from. Jayson Orvis, the author of the post-apocalyptic thriller, has a 300-acre doomsday compound matching the theme, according to a report from PEOPLE. Orvis has spent more than a decade on transforming the property located in Bountiful, Utah, into a self-supporting sanctuary which can shelter 200 people in the event of a civilisation-ending catastrophe. The property, home to the multimillionaire, his wife and three of his seven kids comes with a complete armoury, a machine shop, greenhouses, butchery and a massive storeroom filled with everything from medical textbooks to portable radios and leather-working tools.The location is also the set for his similar themed TV show, Angel Studios' 'Homestead: The Series', which recently returned for Season 2. The 57-year-old entrepreneur's property also boasts a "food forest" that grows fruits and vegetables without pesticides or synthetic fertilisers. “We have more asparagus and raspberries than we can pick,” he told PEOPLE. “We don’t have cattle, but we have wild deer, turkey, elk, goats, rabbits and chickens — natural meat that lives a full life and then we harvest it,” he added.Orvis is admittedly very interested in survival amid catastrophe but he believes that doomsday prepping can be less "dark, nihilistic, and antisocial." He co-wrote the post-apocalyptic thriller Black Autumn book series that was spun off into the feature film Homestead and now a TV series.The only thing that Orvis' property doesn't have is a massive blast-resistant underground concrete bunker which is the first thing secured by billionaires like Mark Zuckerberg in preparations for the end times. But the idea of relying on a fortified bunker to survive the end of civilisation isn't thinking big enough, he said to the outlet. “It’s like a weird prepper idea from the Cold War,” he said. “If you’re going to be right at ground zero [it might make sense] — but up here, you don’t need to bury yourself in the ground. And even if you did, what are you gonna have once you emerge from the ground?”If the apocalypse arrives and the society collapses, Orvis and his group of family, friends, medical experts, master gardeners, beekeepers, Navy SEALs, and even a few Afghan refugee commandos would retreat behind the gates of his compound, with its stockpile of 110,000 pounds of grain, a freshwater well and a massive array of electricity-generating solar panels.“We’ll be super well defended and we’ll also do the best we can to share and to help our neighbours along,” said Orvis, who calculated that the group could survive “indefinitely” on their cache of supplies and what they can cultivate from the land.Besides preparing for civilisation’s end, Orvis said he was determined to “redefine what preparedness means.” “One would think that it’s every man for themselves, kill or be killed [when society collapses],” Orvis said. “Jeff told me that after having seen what happened in places like Haiti, Iraq and Afghanistan, it isn’t the people with the belt-fed machine guns who survive. It’s the people who bind together and form powerful, strong communities,” he said mentioning his co-writer Jeff Kirkham, a former Green Beret with multiple tours in Afghanistan and Iraq.Orvis made a fortune more than 15 years ago after his credit repair business was acquired by an equity fund. “My dad was a firefighter turned metal fabricator and a prepper,” he said, adding that he wrote his first article for a prepper journal at the age of 15. “I grew up with chickens, bees, rabbits and gardens in the backyard, so preparedness has always been kind of a hobby,” he said.After selling his business in 2010, Orvis began focusing on philanthropic work and soon found himself “called to help” former special forces soldiers, using his social marketing skills to help them launch entrepreneurial ventures like Black Rifle Coffee and the self-reliance website retailer Readyman. This is when he met Kirkham, and the two began brainstorming ideas for their faith-based post-apocalyptic series that now includes 10 books and, said Orvis, has allowed them to tell stories of “high peril and high hope.”By then, Orvis had already begun transforming his massive property into a paradise for the point of no return. “We had a garden and food storage, but we didn’t have goats, rabbits, chickens and all this,” recalled Orvis’ wife, Pamela, 57. “So Jayson started digging into it. Before long, everything just snowballed and we took it to the next level.”However, despite all his preparedness and plans, Orvis is "pretty damn sure the world isn't going to collapse." “It is possible, but I think the odds are probably sub-2 or 1% in my lifetime,” he said.You use AI every day. articles.title: Back in Faridabad for nephew's wedding, Singapore-based man shot dead by neighbour over parking dispute; fired 15 rounds
articles.summary: FARIDABAD: A man was shot dead following a dispute over vehicle parking in Sector 21C on the night of Dhanteras, two days before Diwali.
articles.body: FARIDABAD: A man was shot dead following a dispute over vehicle parking in Sector 21C on the night of Dhanteras, two days before Diwali.The deceased, identified as Paramjeet Dhankar, was allegedly shot by his neighbour, Mohan alias Monu Sharma, who is accused of opening fire with his licensed pistol.According to police, the accused fired around 15-16 rounds, of which three to four bullets hit Paramjeet, killing him on the spot.Paramjeet lived on the first floor of house number 641 with his wife, son and daughter. He was employed with a private company in Singapore.He had returned to Faridabad just two days before the incident to attend his nephew's wedding, scheduled for November 24. He originally belonged to Hisar.Police said Paramjeet had returned home from the gym around 8pm when an argument broke out between him and Mohan, who lived on the third floor of the same building, over vehicle parking. Police are also investigating whether the dispute was linked to a pet dog.The argument escalated, following which the accused allegedly opened fire at Paramjeet.According to police, the two families had a history of disputes. Five days before the incident, the accused had allegedly abused Paramjeet's son.After the shooting, Mohan fled with his family. On receiving information, teams from the local police, crime branch and forensic science laboratory (FSL) reached the spot. Empty cartridges were recovered from the crime scene.Police are searching for the accused.Prahlad Kumar, SHO of Surajkund police station, confirmed the incident and said teams were investigating the case and searching for the accused.He said the accused had fired around 15 rounds.Stay updated with the latest Faridabad news. articles.title: Mumbai woman wins Rs 9.6  lakh in a sleep internship and a sponsored vacation after a 60-day competition, and it just tested her bedtime routine and creativity
articles.summary: Sometimes a good night’s sleep can give you more than a fresh start to the day.
articles.body: Sometimes a good night’s sleep can give you more than a fresh start to the day. For Jiniya Chatterjee from Mumbai, it brought ₹9.6 lakh and a sponsored vacation.She was named the winner of the fifth season of Wakefit’s Sleep Internship, a two-month contest that brought together 10 participants from across India.But earning money purely for sleeping sounds bizarre, right?But sleeping is not just limited to taking rest; activities like this are now used to track sleep patterns and improve daily scores.Here’s how the competition worked and how Jiniya emerged at the top.Mumbai's Jiniya Chatterjee wins ₹9.6 lakh in a fitness brand’s sleep internshipSleeping well just earned a woman from Mumbai ₹9.6 lakh and a holiday. According to Aaj Tak, Jiniya Chatterjee was named the winner of the fifth Sleep Internship, run by mattress and sleep-products company Wakefit. Besides the cash, she received a sponsored vacation. The competition lasted two months and drew participants from across India. Wakefit's own website describes her as a singer, performer and entrepreneur who fiercely protects her bedtime.What is the idea behind the internship?More than 2 lakh people applied this season, and 10 were selected. For 60 days, they tracked their sleep, kept a regular routine and took on weekly challenges to climb the leaderboard. Wakefit's terms say each intern gets ₹1 lakh for completing the programme, while the winner can receive up to ₹10 lakh plus a vacation. To be eligible, applicants must be at least 22 years old, and Jiniya's ₹9.6 lakh falls inside that limit.The weekly tasks were not only about sleepingThe participants were also tested for their creativity. In Sleep Cinema, participants recreated scenes from popular films with a sleep twist. Sleep Bingo asked them to review their sleeping habits over a week. In the Undercover Sleep Mission, they had to say "blanket" or "pillow" ten times in a conversation without anyone noticing. Each week's best performer was named Pro Sleeper of the Week.After 60 days, Ratnagiri Manikandan, Jiniya Chatterjee and Mehek Khot emerged as the top three; apart from that, Karim Khan from Hyderabad joined them as a wildcard entry after winning the most weekly creative challenges. That made four finalists for the grand finale, called Big Bedd, which followed the format of a reality show.The finale mixed games with the real testIn the Memory Foam Challenge, contestants rebuilt a bedroom setup from reference images, testing memory, observation and teamwork. In the Sleep Auction, they bid for what they needed to build their sleeping space, including pillows, blankets, air-conditioning settings, lighting and sound. It was like reality television, with contestants moving from one task to the next before finally heading to bed. Their sleep scores from that last night then played an important role in choosing the winner.Prize money has crept up over the yearsWakefit's earlier announcement notes that last year's champion, Pooja Madhav Wavhal from Pune, won ₹9.1 lakh in Season 4. According to MediaInfoline, Wakefit co-founder Chaitanya Ramalingegowda said that after five seasons, people's enthusiasm for "making sleep a priority" keeps amazing the company.Get the latest movie news, reviews, and celebrity updates.
